newsitem.title: FINLAND: SWIMMING-SILANTIEV AND SIEVINEN STAR IN WORLD CUP.
newsitem.headline: SWIMMING-SILANTIEV AND SIEVINEN STAR IN WORLD CUP.

text.p: Ukraine's Denis Silantiev equalled a European record and world champion Jani Sievinen completed a hat-trick of individual medleys on the final day of a World Cup swimming meeting on Thursday.

Silantiev, who had already taken the 200 metres butterfly on Wednesday, clocked 24.81 in the 100 metres butterfly to match German Michael Gross's seven-year-old record and finish comfortably clear of second-placed Vesa Hanski of Finland.

Sievinen, back in international competition after a break following his disappointing Olympics last July, swept to victory in the 200 metres individual medley in one minute 58.52 seconds, over five seconds ahead of the opposition.

The Finn, who holds three world short-course records and one long-course mark but managed only a single silver medal in Atlanta, won Wednesday's 100 metres and 400 metres medleys by equally wide margins in a convincing return to form.
The Espoo event will be his only appearance in the World Cup series this year as he is concentrating his training on the European long-course championships in Seville, Spain, in August.

China's four-strong women's team continued to impress, with Mi Tong adding victories in the 50 and 200 metres breaststroke to Wednesday's 100-metre breaststroke win and Chen Yan taking the 400 metres individual medley after earlier winning the 200 metres event.
But Yan -- he also leads the World Cup backstroke rankings -- and Tong will both make a last World Cup appearance for this year in Malmo, Sweden.
Thursday's women's butterfly events were dominated by Dane Mette Jakobsen, with victories at 50 and 200 metres.
